p1.scene: Two pictures of the same beach. Left: the examiner's picture. Right: your picture.
p1.examiner: Look at the two pictures. Here the sun is shining, but here it is cloudy. What other differences can you see?
differences: In your picture the boy has got a green kite, but in my picture it is yellow.
In your picture there are two boats in the sea, but in my picture there is one.
In your picture the woman is reading a book, but in my picture she is sleeping.
In your picture the girl is wearing a hat, but in my picture she isn't.
In your picture there is a crab on the sand, but in my picture there is a shell.

p2.title: Peter and the tent
p2.examiner_open: These pictures show a story. It's called 'Peter and the tent'. Look at the pictures first. Peter and his dad are camping in the mountains. It's the evening and they are putting up their tent. Now you tell the story.
frames: Peter and his dad are camping in the mountains. In the evening they put up their tent next to a river.
At night it starts to rain and the wind is very strong. The tent falls down and Peter and his dad get wet.
They run to the car and sleep there. Peter is laughing because his dad's hair is very wet.
In the morning the sun is shining again. They put up the tent and cook breakfast on a fire.

p1: Part One. Look at the picture. Listen and look. There is one example.
Grandma, look at this photo of the station. We're all waiting for the train.
Who's the girl with the purple suitcase? She's got sunglasses.
That's Jane, my cousin. She always wears sunglasses on holiday.
Can you see the line? This is an example. Now you listen and draw lines.
And who's the boy on the bench? He's eating something.
That's Charlie. He's eating a sandwich. He's always hungry!
Can you see the woman with the big map?
Yes, Aunt Sue. She wanted to find the hotel on the map.
Who's the man sleeping? He's got a newspaper on his face!
That's Uncle Peter. He got up very early, so he was tired.
Ha ha! I hope he didn't miss the train.
Look at the girl with the small dog.
Yes, that's Mary and her dog, Biscuit. He went on holiday too.
And the boy pointing at the clock? Who's that?
That's Nick. He said 'The train is late!' He looked at the clock every minute.
Now listen to Part One again.
p2: Part Two. Listen and look. There is one example.
Dad, where are we going on holiday this year?
We're going to a lake in the mountains. It's called Lake Silver.
Yes, very big and very blue.
Can you see the answer? Now you listen and write.
No, it's too far. We're going by train. It takes four hours.
How many days are we staying there?
Where are we going to sleep?
In a hotel next to the lake. It's called the Star Hotel. S-T-A-R.
The Star Hotel. Has it got a swimming pool?
Can we go on the lake?
Yes, we can go in a boat. A small boat with a motor.
A boat! Can I drive it?
No, but you can help me.
What do I need to take?
Your coat. It's cold in the mountains in the evening, even in summer.
My coat. OK. And my camera!
Now listen to Part Two again.
p3: Part Three. Listen and look. There is one example.
Ben is telling his teacher what each person in his family did on holiday. What did each person do?
Did you have a good holiday, Ben?
Yes, Miss Green. We went to the sea. I swam every day. The water was warm.
Can you see the letter G? Now you listen and write a letter in each box.
And what did your dad do?
He went fishing every morning in a small boat. He caught a big fish on the last day!
My mum took hundreds of photos. She's got a new camera. She took photos of the sea, the boats, the birds… everything!
Did your grandfather go with you?
Yes, but he didn't swim. He was tired, so he slept under a big umbrella every afternoon.
My sister did something very difficult. She climbed a mountain with my uncle! It took all day.
Climbing a mountain! She's very strong.
And your aunt? Did she climb too?
No! She went shopping in the town every day. She bought lots of presents and a big hat.
Ha ha! Everybody did something different.
Now listen to Part Three again.
p4: Part Four. Look at the pictures. Listen and look. There is one example.
Where did Lucy go on holiday?
Did you go to the beach on holiday, Lucy?
No, Grandpa. We went to the mountains. It was cold, but beautiful.
No, there weren't any cities. Just mountains and lakes.
Can you see the tick? Now you listen and tick the box.
One. What time does the train leave?
Mum, does our train leave at eight o'clock?
No, that's the bus. Our train leaves at ten.
Ten o'clock. So we can have breakfast first.
Two. What is Grandma going to buy?
Grandma, are you going to buy sunglasses for the beach?
No, I've got sunglasses. I want to buy a hat. A big one.
No, I've got lots of T-shirts.
Three. What did Paul see in the sea?
Paul, did you see a shark when you went on the boat?
No, Mum! I saw a dolphin. It jumped next to the boat.
No, it was small. It was a dolphin.
Dad, I can't find my camera. Is it in the car?
No, I looked in the car. Is it in your bag?
No… Oh! Here it is. On my bed, under the towel.
Good. Put it in your bag now.
Five. What is Dad cooking for dinner?
Dad, are you cooking fish for dinner?
No, we had fish yesterday. Tonight it's pasta.
Now listen to Part Four again.
p5: Part Five. Look at the picture. Listen and look. There is one example.
Look at this picture of the campsite. Can you see the small tent next to the tree?
Can you see the green tent? This is an example. Now you listen and colour and write.
Now, can you see the bird on the tree?
There's a cup on the table. Can I colour it?
Can you see the boy fishing in the river? He's got a fish on his line.
Yes! Shall I colour the fish?
Yes. There's a flag on the big tent. Write the word 'happy' on it. H-A-P-P-Y.
Happy. On the flag. OK, I'm writing it.
And now the girl with the camera. Can you see her hat?
Yes. Can I colour it blue?
Now listen to Part Five again.
